items.content: She woke to a quality of light that was wrong — too bright too early, too diffuse, coming from everywhere at once. Then the silence: no traffic, no birds, only a muffled compression of the world. She crossed to the window and found that overnight the city had been revised. Every edge softened. Every distinction erased. The street below her was unrecognizable and, for reasons she could not name, that felt like relief.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "waking up to find snow has fallen overnight". AI text often produces grammatically perfect sentences with slightly generic emotional beats — look for overly balanced structure and lack of truly surprising word choices.

items.content: The cinema was almost dark even before the lights went fully down. She had chosen the end of the row deliberately, and sat with her coat still on and her popcorn untouched, looking at the blank screen that was not yet blank but only waiting. There is something about the two minutes before a film, she thought, that is better than almost anything: pure expectation, nothing yet decided, the story still infinite.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "sitting alone in a cinema before the film starts". Notice the even pacing and absence of the kinds of small errors or tonal shifts that appear in prose written under genuine emotional pressure.

items.content: The last page arrived and she turned it slowly, as though her reluctance alone could postpone the ending. She had been in the book for eleven days, carrying it through her mornings, her commutes, her evenings at the kitchen table. Now the characters would continue without her, in some dimension she could not enter. She closed the cover and sat for a while in the particular grief of a world completed — finished, unrevisable, over.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the feeling of finishing a book you didn't want to end". The polished structure and conceptually inventive metaphors are characteristic of language model output.
A dramatic mountain landscape captured on camera. The physical scale cues and real atmospheric perspective mark this as human photography.

items.content: You don't know about me without you have read a book by the name of The Adventures of Tom Sawyer; but that ain't no matter.
items.explanation: Huck Finn's vernacular opening, 1884. The deliberate grammatical 'incorrectness' is an intentional human artistic choice that AI trained on edited prose rarely produces naturally.
items.source: Mark Twain — Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1884)
